legend: You are given an array of n%%ZSMJ0%% nonnegative integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ1%%.
Let m%%ZSMJ2%% be a variable that is initialized to 0%%ZSMJ3%%, Jellyfish will perform the following operation n%%ZSMJ4%% times:
select an index i%%ZSMJ5%% (1≤i≤|a|%%ZSMJ6%%) and delete ai%%ZSMJ7%% from a%%ZSMJ8%%.
Now Jellyfish wants to know the minimum possible final value of m%%ZSMJ11%% if he performs all the operations optimally.
†%%ZSMJ12%% The MEX (minimum excluded) of an array is the smallest non-negative integer that does not belong to the array. For instance:
The MEX of [2,2,1]%%ZSMJ13%% is 0%%ZSMJ14%%, because 0%%ZSMJ15%% does not belong to the array.
The MEX of [3,1,0,1]%%ZSMJ16%% is 2%%ZSMJ17%%, because 0%%ZSMJ18%% and 1%%ZSMJ19%% belong to the array, but 2%%ZSMJ20%% does not.
The MEX of [0,3,1,2]%%ZSMJ21%% is 4%%ZSMJ22%% because 0%%ZSMJ23%%, 1%%ZSMJ24%%, 2%%ZSMJ25%%, and 3%%ZSMJ26%% belong to the array, but 4%%ZSMJ27%% does not.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ28%% (1≤t≤5000%%ZSMJ29%%). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ30%% (1≤n≤5000%%ZSMJ31%%) — the size of the array.
The second line of each test case contains n%%ZSMJ32%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ33%% (0≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ34%%) — the integers in the array.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ35%% over all test cases does not exceed 5000%%ZSMJ36%%.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum value of m%%ZSMJ37%% if the operations are performed optimally.
note: In the first test case, we delete elements from a%%ZSMJ38%% in the following order: [5,2,1,0,3,0,4,0]→[5,2,0,3,0,4,0]→[5,2,0,3,4,0]→[5,2,3,4,0]→[5,2,3,4]→[5,2,4]→[2,4]→[4]→[ ]%%ZSMJ39%%. The value of m%%ZSMJ40%% will be 1+1+1+0+0+0+0+0=3%%ZSMJ41%%.
